lesson.title: How People Live
lesson.summary: Homes around the world, how food gets from the farm to our plate, and how travel and daily life have changed.
learning_objectives: Describe different kinds of homes and why they differ
Follow food from farm to plate
Compare transport and life long ago with today

standards.text: Changes within living memory, where appropriate, aspects of change in national life

success_criteria: I can name different kinds of homes
I can tell the journey of a roti from the farm

lesson.real_life: Seeing a farm or a mill, riding a bus or train, and asking grandparents what life was like when they were small.

blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: how do people live, and how has life changed?

We will visit homes, farms and the past.
blocks.say: Welcome, people watcher! Today's big question is: how do people live, and how has life changed? We will look at homes around the world, follow a roti all the way from the farm, and find out how people travelled long ago. This is a game, not a test. Let's go!

blocks.caption: Homes around the world look different.

terms.meaning: All the men, women and children in the world.

blocks.markdown:
A **home** is a place where we live and feel safe.

Homes can be houses, **flats**, **tents** or mud-brick homes.
blocks.say: Where do you live? Your home is the place where you sleep, eat and feel safe. But homes are not all the same! Some families live in houses made of bricks. Some live in flats, high up in a tall building. Some people, who move from place to place, live in tents. And in many villages, families live in homes made of mud bricks. Every one of these is a home.

scenes.caption: A brick house.
scenes.say: Here is a house made of bricks. Many families in towns and cities live in houses like this.

scenes.caption: Flats in a tall building.
scenes.say: Here are flats. Many families live in one tall building, each family in its own flat.

scenes.caption: A tent can be moved.
scenes.say: Here is a tent. People who move from place to place, with their animals, can pack up their tent and take it with them.

scenes.caption: A mud-brick home.
scenes.say: And here is a mud-brick home, in a village. Mud and straw are free and everywhere, and they keep the home cool in summer.

question.prompt: Which kind of home can be packed up and carried away?
question.hint: Think of people who move from place to place.
question.explanation: A tent can be packed up and taken with you.

blocks.markdown:
People build homes to suit the **weather** and what is nearby.

A steep roof lets snow slide off. Thick walls keep a home cool.
blocks.say: Why do homes look different in different places? Because of the weather, and because of what is nearby. In a snowy place, a house often has a steep roof, so the heavy snow slides off. In a very hot place, a home has thick walls and shady spaces to keep the heat out. A home keeps us warm, cool, dry and safe, whatever the weather.

scenes.caption: Snowy place: a steep roof.
scenes.say: In a snowy place the roof is steep. Watch the snow slide off and fall to the ground, so the roof does not get too heavy.

scenes.caption: Hot place: thick walls keep it cool.
scenes.say: In a hot place the walls are thick and the windows are small. This keeps the home cool inside.

question.prompt: Thick walls can help keep a home cool in hot weather.
question.explanation: Thick walls keep the heat out.

People build homes to suit the weather

blocks.markdown:
A **farmer** grows food in a **field**.

When the wheat is ready, the farmer cuts it. This is the **harvest**.
blocks.say: Have you ever wondered where your roti comes from? It starts on a farm! A farmer plants wheat seeds in a field. The sun shines and the rain falls, and the seeds grow into tall golden wheat. When the wheat is ready, the farmer cuts it. That is called the harvest.

scenes.caption: A seed is planted.
scenes.say: First, the farmer plants a tiny seed in the field.

scenes.caption: The seed grows into wheat.
scenes.say: The sun shines, the rain falls, and the seed grows into golden wheat.

scenes.caption: Harvest time.
scenes.say: Then comes the harvest. The farmer cuts the wheat, with a tractor or a sickle.

question.prompt: What do we call cutting the wheat when it is ready?
question.hint: It happens at the end of the growing time.
question.explanation: Harvest means cutting the crop when it is ready.

blocks.markdown:
The **mill** grinds wheat into **flour**.

Flour and water make **dough**. Cooked dough becomes a roti.
blocks.say: Now the wheat goes on a journey. A lorry takes it to a mill. The mill grinds the wheat into a soft powder called flour. Then someone mixes the flour with water to make dough. The dough is rolled flat and cooked on a hot tawa. And now we have a roti, ready to eat!

scenes.caption: Wheat goes to the mill.
scenes.say: The wheat goes by lorry to the mill.

scenes.caption: The mill makes flour.
scenes.say: The mill grinds the wheat into soft white flour.

scenes.caption: Flour becomes dough, then roti.
scenes.say: Mix the flour with water to make dough, and cook it on the tawa. It puffs up into a warm roti!

blocks.markdown:
Long ago, people travelled on foot or rode **camels** and horses.

Then came trains and cars, and now aeroplanes. Ways of travelling are called **transport**.
blocks.say: How do you get to school? Maybe by car, by bus or on foot. Long ago, there were no cars. People walked, or rode on camels and horses, or sat in carts pulled by animals. Then trains came, with big engines and long carriages. Later came cars, and then aeroplanes that fly across the sky.

scenes.caption: Long ago: camels.
scenes.say: Long ago, people travelled by camel. A camel can carry heavy things across the desert.

scenes.caption: Then: trains.
scenes.say: Then trains were built. A train can carry lots of people and things very far.

scenes.caption: Today: cars and aeroplanes.
scenes.say: After that came cars and buses, and today we also fly in aeroplanes, so a very long journey takes only a few hours!

blocks.markdown:
Older people remember life **long ago**. This is **living memory**.

Their stories show how life has changed.
blocks.say: Here is a secret way to find out about the past. Ask your grandparents, or an older person in your family! They remember what life was like when they were small. What they remember is called living memory. Their stories show us how life has changed.

blocks.alt: Grandparents remember what life was like long ago.
blocks.caption: Grandparents remember what life was like long ago.
blocks.say: Here are a grandmother and a grandfather. They have so many stories to tell.

blocks.prompt: What could you ask a grandparent about when they were small?
blocks.answer_markdown: You could ask: How did you get to school? What games did you play? What food did you eat? Did you have a mobile phone?
blocks.say: Now it is your turn to think. What would you like to ask your grandparent? Have a think, then tap to see some ideas.

question.prompt: Grandparents can tell us what life was like long ago.
question.hint: They remember when they were young.
question.explanation: Older people remember, and their stories teach us about the past.

blocks.markdown:
Many things have **changed**. A telephone used to have a wire. Today we carry mobile phones.

Some things stay the same: families share meals and children play.
blocks.say: Lots of things have changed. When your grandparents were small, many families had only one telephone in the house, with a wire. Some had no television. Today we can talk to someone far away on a mobile phone, using a picture on a screen! Some things have not changed at all. Families still share meals, and children still love to play.

blocks.alt: A telephone with a wire long ago, and a mobile phone today.
blocks.caption: A telephone with a wire long ago, and a mobile phone today.
blocks.say: Look at these two telephones. One has a wire, and one fits in your pocket. That is how much things have changed!
